guards.what: The applier is a potion, and the potion KIND has no audit tier
guards.rationale: NARROWED 2026-07-26 (review fix pass). The old rationale said "what is waived is only the REACHABILITY of its one applier". That was wrong twice over: it is logically incompatible with this record tagging any hook LIVE (LIVE is itself a reachability claim), and it is stale -- Flex Potion is ported and POOL-REGISTERED, so the power is reachable in the sim today whether or not the potion tier is ever written. What is genuinely out of scope, and all this waiver now claims, is the potion UNIT's own record: potions are a deferred kind by Perry's deferral (the shared audit contract's Global scope section) and there is no audit/records/potion/ tier for Flex Potion to live in, so nothing here judges the potion's own fidelity (cost, targeting, belt behaviour). REACHABILITY IS ESTABLISHED, not waived: the sim ports the potion at potions.py:108-124, @register_potion puts it in ALL_POTIONS, and it is in the generation pool at potion_pools.py:50 (common). The POWER is audited in full above and every liveness label on this record stands on its own evidence. Same correction at all seven power records carrying this guard (power/buffer, power/clarity, power/flex_potion, power/gigantification, power/radiance, power/shackling_potion, power/speed_potion) so the mechanism keeps one verdict at every site per binding rule 3.

notes: HARNESS, not a verdict (moved out of `guards` 2026-07-26 in the review fix pass): harness.py's list_overrides enumerated ONE hook for this unit -- OriginModel, the only member the .cs file itself declares -- where the unit needs six, because it did not follow the C# base class. The five inherited hooks in this record's `hooks` section were added by hand; validation accepts extra keys. This is defect 2b of the stream report's section 8, found by half A on six TemporaryStrengthPower subclasses and reproducing on both previously unauditable potion powers. It used to be recorded as a guard verdicted `waiver`, which was wrong: a tooling defect is not a scope exclusion, and binding rule 1 reserves `waiver` for genuinely out-of-scope material (multiplayer / presentation / ascension / other characters). It is a note about the audit apparatus, not a sim-vs-game finding, so it carries no verdict and does not enter this record's rollup.
